purpose: Machine-readable decomposition of this repo's own validation so failures are attributable to a named validator, and so a repair that genuinely fixes a validator's defect can be declared next to it.

profiles.release: Every leaf validator reached by `npm run validate:release`, plus the query-atlas gate that guards the evidence the atlas publishes against.
profiles.core: The page-level matrix only. Fast pass for content edits.
profiles.lane: Validators that need the GitHub API and a token. Run as named steps in deploy-distribution.yml on every event it has, not from validate:release.

repair_policy: repair_command may only be declared when the command regenerates the exact artifact whose defect the validator detects. A repair is never declared to make an unrelated failure disappear; validators whose failures require human judgement are left with no repair and are reported by name.

validators.detects: No /about, an /about that is unpublished or noindex, a published page that does not link it, an About page that omits the publisher, the Terms, the Privacy Policy, the Google Business Profile, the Facebook Page or a service's starting price from the data, one that quotes a price the data files do not hold, one carrying a review, rating, award, certification, insurance, years-in-business or job-count claim this repository holds no record of, or one that prints the legal entity's name (owner-approved 2026-10-18: only the Terms and the Privacy Policy may).

Published pages missing the blocks an answer engine needs to quote and act on them: a direct answer (a labelled block, or a lead paragraph not below 75% of 80 characters), an h1 that carries the query (not below 75% of 11 characters; length floors via scripts/lib/length_floor.js, never a ceiling), tables without empty cells, and one quote-request conversion path. Coverage for checklist, comparison table, concrete numbers, named sources, FAQ and JSON-LD is measured and reported.
Required files, canonicals, entity footers, legal links, internal hrefs, JSON-LD wellformedness and llms.txt extraction surfaces across every published page.
validators.no_repair_reason: Composite page-level matrix. Its failures (missing canonical, broken href, missing footer, malformed JSON-LD) are authored defects with no single regenerator. The one derived-artifact defect it also covers - sitemap desync - is attributed precisely by the sitemap-coverage validator below, which does carry a repair.

validators.detects: An internal href that resolves to no published file, counting clean URLs (<path>.html), directory indexes and _redirects sources as resolved.
validators.no_repair_reason: A broken href is either a typo or a page that was never built. Both are authored defects; a regenerator would only paper over the second.

validators.detects: KPI claims not backed by the observed surfacing ledger.
validators.no_repair_reason: The ledger is measured evidence. Nothing in the repo may generate it, and generating it would be fabrication.

validators.detects: Query evidence missing a tier or source_type, a publishable atlas entry on a non-publishable tier or with no volume, and a query_atlas.json that is absent or stale against the evidence file.
validators.repair_rationale: build_query_atlas.mjs writes data/authority_scale/query_atlas.json from data/queries/evidence/evidence_queries.json. The validator's own failure text says 'run the atlas build first'. This is the pairing that closes the loop after queries:ingest writes new measured T1 evidence.

validators.detects: A published page promising fee-free travel to a town that pays the travel fee, a fee-paying town whose pages never state the fee, a fee-free town with no page, or travel.line naming a different set of towns than travel.includedAreas.
validators.no_repair_reason: A false price is a copy and data decision, not a regenerable artifact. The failure names the town and the page; whoever fixes it decides whether the town belongs on travel.includedAreas (the owner's call) or whether the page's wording is wrong (the generator's).

validators.detects: Stray, orphaned or non-canonical files in the published tree.
Deposit shortcuts open a confirm screen without recording; confirmed payments reuse the ledger and history, clear holds, retain partial balances, and agree across the email, feed and day list.

Corporate form storage and owner labels; email signatures; token auth; campaign cutoff, paid booking stop, atomic daily limits, suppression, company takeover, do-not-contact and follow-up guards; conservative MIME inbound routing; private deployment sender restrictions.

pnp-mailer fetch() sends nothing without the shared-secret header (missing, wrong, partial, or an unconfigured Worker -> 401); the harness's fake MAILER refuses headerless calls so every mail-sending validator proves its caller sends it.

PART: a page or llms file that says "insured"; the legal name Kerseta in visible text outside the Terms and the Privacy Policy; Terms without "Reply STOP to opt out" and "Message and data rates may apply"; Privacy without #privacy-choices and the Microsoft Clarity opt-out; a page that does not link the Privacy Policy.

Clarity recording outside a form/checkout page, a conversion page missing its loader, duplicate loaders, or an installer that does not remove legacy tags and stay idempotent. Exercises the real installer with fixtures.
validators.no_repair_reason: Run scripts/install_clarity.js inside an exact-route thaw/refreeze scope for frozen pages; an unattended repair must not mutate accepted output outside that scope.

validators.detects: A page whose structured data states a datePublished or dateModified and shows it nowhere a reader can see, a visible date the structured data does not state, a date line on a page that claims none, or a date line placed above the lead paragraph where it displaces the page's direct answer.
A sitemap <lastmod> that is a run-date stamp, moves on a chrome-only change, or disagrees with the lastmod ledger and the content on disk (two-run fixture).

PART: a published city x service page that does not state the data-file prices (games.json day/weekend rate, grazing tier from-prices, porch from-price, the sibling block from-prices), or generator output that differs from a fresh scripts/generators/build_area_pages.js run.
PART: a $ amount on /faq/ that is not a price in services.json, porch_packages.json or games.json; a travel answer that does not name every city in areas.json and the $75 travel fee.
PART: a hotel anchor page (or the hub it folded into) that does not say "Porch & Party is not affiliated with <hotel>".

PART (rules 1 and 1b, email_off): a mailto: anchor outside <!--email_off--> or an email address in rendered text outside it, both of which Cloudflare rewrites into a 404 /cdn-cgi/l/email-protection link.
